emergent_bug.violated_requirement: ρ = atomic([access(napi->rx_count/rx_list)]) from thread_a (its gro_normal_list update of the NAPI normal-GRO list must not be interleaved with a conflicting access of the same NAPI)
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@napi_busy_loop:6348 = access(napi->rx_count) via gro_normal_list(napi) on the busy-poll side
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: the TUN write path invokes napi_gro_frags in process (writev) context, bypassing the NAPI poll scheduling discipline (NAPI_STATE_SCHED) that normally keeps gro_normal_list a single-accessor; busy-poll concurrently polls the same registered NAPI. No lock/order serializes the two accesses to this NAPI's GRO list
emergent_bug.category_rationale: ρ is atomic over a single access; two concurrent conflicting accesses to rx_count with no synchronization → data race

fix_maps_to: netif_napi_add() -> netif_tx_napi_add() in tun_napi_init() marks the NAPI as tx-only, excluding it from busy-poll's napi_id-based polling. This ELIMINATES thread_b's access (makes concurrent=false) rather than adding a contract-site sync; it is not expressible as any of {serialize, order, counts} — the fix removes the interleaving instead of establishing ρ
recall_risk_notes: Three risks: (1) object identity must be grounded across napi_busy_loop's napi_id global-hash lookup back to tfile->napi; static aliasing likely cannot prove same_location, risking an FN at grounding. (2) NAPI poll serialization (sched bit / epoch) is subtle — an LLM may wrongly conclude gro_normal_list is always serialized by the NAPI poll discipline and ADD a bogus order/serialize guarantee, suppressing the report. (3) The real fix is a registration-policy change that removes concurrency, which our closed algebra cannot express as an added guarantee; our framing relies on 'no guarantee establishes ρ' (true here) but diverges from the maintainer's mental model.
